name: NY-14
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+19 district partisanship in a favorable Democratic environment
Ocasio-Cortez's massive financial advantage ($37M raised, $17M on hand vs ~$0.4M)
Incumbency and high national profile; markets price her at 99%
model.rationale: The D+19 lean, a Democratic-tilting national environment, and incumbency point to a margin near the low 30s, while the challenger's negligible fundraising and cash confirm no serious threat; prediction markets price a Democratic win at 99%. A modest discount for the incumbent's polarizing profile keeps the expected margin in the high 20s.
model.watch: Any surprise primary upset or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the expected margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez seeks another term in a New York City district that leans Democratic by about 19 points. She enters the general election with overwhelming resources, having raised more than $37 million and holding over $17 million on hand, while Republican Diamant Hysenaj has raised only about $400,000 with almost no cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

Prediction markets give Ocasio-Cortez roughly a 99 percent chance of winning, and no public general-election polling suggests the race is competitive. The combination of district partisanship, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes this one of the safest Democratic House seats on the ballot, with the only real uncertainty being the size of the winning margin.
